criteria.statement: OWN THE FRAME — A SINGLE PRIORITIZED PER-FRAME BIND THAT ALL CAMERA SYSTEMS COMPOSE THROUGH. The camera takes full custom per-frame ownership rather than leaving the stock follow camera to run, and a PASS requires committing to BOTH load-bearing ownership facts: (1) the camera's per-frame write is taken over by the build's own code — either CameraType=Enum.CameraType.Scriptable is set so the default camera cannot silently overwrite the CFrame, OR the build NAMES that it is deliberately riding the stock camera via Humanoid.CameraOffset to inherit free occlusion/input (a valid senior non-invasive choice); AND (2) that per-frame work is driven by a SINGLE shared bind at the camera render slot — RunService:BindToRenderStep(name, Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, fn) (or +1 to win) — through which the build's camera systems (follow/smoother and any offset/effect layers) run, NOT a bare unprioritized RenderStepped/.Stepped/.Heartbeat connection and NOT each effect on its own ad-hoc connection. The discriminator is committing to custom prioritized frame ownership that the whole camera rig writes through: a build that lets the stock follow camera run untouched (the beginner default), writes the CFrame on an unprioritized RenderStepped/Heartbeat, or forgets Scriptable and fights the default camera, FAILS. A build that takes ownership (Scriptable or named CameraOffset) AND drives its camera systems through one BindToRenderStep at RenderPriority.Camera PASSES. Full marks ADD the deeper correctness facts the bind contract needs to be airtight: Camera.Focus written every frame (it is NOT auto-tracked under Scriptable and drives lighting/streaming/LOD), reversible restore (CameraType=Custom + CameraSubject re-pointed at the Humanoid) on hand-back, the explicit Input(100)->Camera(200)->Character(300) ordering rationale, and the +1-to-win detail.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: This is the entry gate every above-generic camera behavior (modes, spring follow, reactive FOV, shake, lock-on) composes onto — the stock 'Custom' follow camera exposes none of those hooks and is the beginner default. The criterion stays above mere presence because the non-obvious move is routing the ENTIRE camera rig through one prioritized bind at RenderPriority.Camera (so the write runs after input is sampled, right before render, eliminating one-frame-stale jitter) instead of leaving the stock camera running or scattering effects across unprioritized connections that fight. The earlier version over-indexed on two facts an artifact-level summary rarely spells out (every-frame Focus writes and reversible restore), so a fully custom rig that demonstrably owns the frame via BindToRenderStep at Camera priority scored identically to a do-nothing stock camera — zero discrimination. Demoting Focus/restore/ordering to full-marks while keeping 'custom prioritized ownership the rig writes through' as the pass bar restores the separation: a real custom rig clears it, a stock-follow build cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) the build takes over the per-frame write — CameraType=Scriptable set, OR an explicit named decision to ride the stock camera via Humanoid.CameraOffset to inherit occlusion/input — AND (2) the camera systems are driven through a SINGLE bind at Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value (or +1) via RunService:BindToRenderStep, NOT a bare unprioritized RenderStepped/Stepped/Heartbeat and NOT per-effect ad-hoc connections. Camera.Focus updated every frame, reversible restore of CameraType=Custom/CameraSubject on hand-back, the Input->Camera->Character ordering rationale, and the +1-to-win detail are credited toward FULL MARKS only. Letting the stock follow camera run untouched, an unprioritized RenderStepped/Heartbeat write, or forgetting Scriptable while fighting the default camera does NOT satisfy this. Owning the frame via Scriptable/CameraOffset but binding on an unprioritized connection (or vice versa) earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Take ownership of the frame and route the whole camera rig through one prioritized bind: set Workspace.CurrentCamera.CameraType=Enum.CameraType.Scriptable (or, for an offset-only need, deliberately ride the stock camera via Humanoid.CameraOffset and say so), then run the follow/smoother and every offset/effect layer inside a single function bound via RunService:BindToRenderStep(name, Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, fn) — never a bare RenderStepped/Heartbeat and never a separate ad-hoc connection per effect. For full marks also write Camera.Focus every frame (not auto-tracked under Scriptable), restore CameraType=Custom + re-point CameraSubject on hand-back, and order Input(100)->Camera(200)->Character(300).

grading.pass: Commits to both ownership facts: (1) CameraType=Scriptable set (or a named deliberate Humanoid.CameraOffset non-invasive path), AND (2) the camera systems driven through a SINGLE BindToRenderStep at Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value (or +1), NOT a bare unprioritized RenderStepped/Stepped/Heartbeat and NOT scattered per-effect connections. FULL MARKS additionally state Camera.Focus written every frame, reversible restore (CameraType=Custom + CameraSubject re-pointed) on hand-back, the Input(100)->Camera(200)->Character(300) ordering rationale, and the +1-to-win detail.
grading.partial: Takes per-frame ownership (Scriptable or named CameraOffset) but the write is on an unprioritized RenderStepped/Stepped/Heartbeat (no named Camera priority), OR drives a correctly-prioritized BindToRenderStep but never takes ownership (Scriptable absent / unnamed, so the build risks fighting the default camera). One of the two ownership facts present, the other missing.
grading.fail: Lets the stock follow camera run untouched (the beginner default), writes the camera on an unprioritized RenderStepped/Stepped/Heartbeat with no Camera-priority bind, or forgets CameraType=Scriptable and fights the default camera. The non-invasive Humanoid.CameraOffset path counts only when NAMED as a deliberate choice, never when stock-camera fighting is accidental.

criteria.change_reason: The old criterion made every-frame Camera.Focus writes AND reversible restore the REQUIRED pass discriminators ('required for a pass, not partial credit'). Neither is the kind of fact an artifact-level summary enumerates, so the GREAT rig — which demonstrably owns the frame (it states its effects are 'driven on BindToRenderStep at RenderPriority.Camera' atop a full custom spring/mode/shake/lock-on stack) — FAILED for not spelling out Focus/restore, scoring identically to the do-nothing MEAN stock camera. Zero discrimination, the exact defect being fixed. The rewrite keeps the real systems-depth invariant that separates a custom rig from the stock follow (the build takes per-frame OWNERSHIP via Scriptable/named-CameraOffset AND routes its camera systems through one bind at RenderPriority.Camera) as the pass bar, which the GREAT artifact explicitly commits to, while a stock-follow build with no custom prioritized write cannot. Focus, restore, the Input->Camera->Character ordering, and the +1-to-win detail are preserved but moved to FULL MARKS so they reward depth without nuking discrimination.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — LAYERED ADDITIVE COMPOSITION. The camera is structured as a stable BASE pose plus SUMMED, independently-tunable offset layers (shake, bob, recoil kick, lean/ADS micro-sway, FOV deltas) composited ON TOP — camera.CFrame = baseCFrame * shakeCFrame * bobCFrame (and/or routed through Humanoid.CameraOffset in HRP object-space) — rather than each effect rewriting the final CFrame and stomping the others. The discriminator is whether the build commits to base-pose + composable offsets as its architecture: passing requires the build to state (1) a single computed base CFrame each frame, AND (2) at least TWO reactive effects applied as ADDITIVE/multiplicative offsets (CFrame.new(posOffset) * CFrame.Angles(rotOffset), or summed Humanoid.CameraOffset targets) that layer without any one overwriting the base — so shake composes over follow, bob over shake, recoil over both, and each is independently removable/tunable. A build where the final camera CFrame is hard-written each frame so adding a second effect forces a rewrite and the effects fight each other FAILS. A build that commits to base + >=2 summed offset layers PASSES; routing additive effects through HRP-object-space Humanoid.CameraOffset (so they read correctly as the body rotates), a named per-layer tuning knob, and explicit fade-in/out envelopes push toward full marks. A build with exactly one offset layer over the base (no composition demonstrated), or two effects that overwrite rather than sum, earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: Generic tutorials write the final CFrame directly each frame, so adding a second effect (shake on top of follow, then bob on top of shake) forces a rewrite and the layers stomp each other — a world-space offset even smears sideways when the character turns. The award-quality move is treating the camera as base-pose + summed offset CFrames applied via a single bind callback (exactly how CameraShaker hands you a CFrame offset to multiply onto your own base), or routing offsets through Humanoid.CameraOffset which applies in HRP object-space so bob/recoil/lean read correctly through turns. This 'multiply/sum, don't replace' discipline is the structural seam every other camera technique (shake, reactive FOV, lock-on, sway) composes onto; without it the whole category collapses into scattered one-off scripts that fight. Grading the base+>=2-composable-layers commitment keeps it discriminating: a build that demonstrates composition clears it, a build that hard-writes the final CFrame cannot add a second layer without a rewrite.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) a single computed BASE camera CFrame per frame AND (2) >=2 reactive effects applied as additive/multiplicative offsets (baseCFrame * CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(rot), or summed Humanoid.CameraOffset targets) that layer without overwriting the base or each other. HRP-object-space CameraOffset routing, per-layer tuning knobs, and fade envelopes are credited toward full marks. Hard-writing the final CFrame each frame (so a second effect forces a rewrite / stomps the first), or world-space offsets that smear on turn, does NOT satisfy this; a single offset layer, or two effects that overwrite rather than sum, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Compute a stable base CFrame each frame, then composite every reactive effect as an offset on top: camera.CFrame = base * shakeCFrame * bobCFrame (each = CFrame.new(posOffset) * CFrame.Angles(rotOffset)), or route bob/recoil/lean through Humanoid.CameraOffset in HRP object-space so they sum and read correctly as the body rotates. Give each layer its own intensity knob so it is independently tunable and removable — never rewrite the final CFrame per effect.

grading.pass: Commits to base-pose + composable offsets: (1) a single computed BASE camera CFrame per frame AND (2) >=2 reactive effects applied as additive/multiplicative offsets (baseCFrame * CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(rot), or summed Humanoid.CameraOffset targets) that layer without any one overwriting the base or each other. Full marks add HRP-object-space CameraOffset routing, named per-layer tuning knobs, and explicit fade-in/out envelopes.
grading.partial: Base pose present but only ONE offset layer over it (composition not actually demonstrated), OR two effects that overwrite rather than sum (so they stack only by luck of ordering, not by genuine composition).
grading.fail: The final camera CFrame is hard-written each frame so adding a second effect forces a rewrite and the effects fight/stomp each other, or world-space offsets are used that smear sideways when the character turns. No genuine base + summed-offset architecture.

criteria.statement: SMOOTH THE PIVOT, DERIVE THE CFRAME — NEVER LERP THE FINAL POSE. Smoothing is applied to the INTERMEDIATE values (focus/pivot point, zoom distance, shoulder-offset vector, FOV) and the final camera CFrame is DERIVED from those each frame — the build never lerps the final camera CFrame directly toward a moving target. The discriminator is whether the build commits to smoothing intermediates rather than the output pose: passing requires the build to state (1) that the smoothed quantities are the pivot/focus and/or distance and/or offset vector (e.g. cameraOffset = cameraOffset:Lerp(targetOffset, alpha) then applied via PointToWorldSpace; focus smoothed then CFrame.lookAt(camPos, focus)), AND (2) that the camera CFrame is rebuilt from those smoothed inputs (lookAt / fromMatrix / distance-along-look) rather than current.CFrame:Lerp(goalCFrame, a) toward a moving target inside the render step. A build that lerps the final camera CFrame straight at a moving target every render frame (the classic jittery/desynced custom camera, fighting the camera's own state) FAILS. A build that smooths the intermediates and derives the pose PASSES; lerping the offset VECTOR for a glide shoulder-swap (not the CFrame), and a clean lookAt/fromMatrix reconstruction, push toward full marks. A build that smooths some intermediates but still lerps the final CFrame for the follow earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The documented cure for the single most common jittery-BindToRenderStep camera: lerping the final CFrame 'does not look correct in RenderStep, because at this moment the camera already must be at the position' — it fights the camera's own state and produces the classic shaky/desynced custom camera. Smoothing the pivot/offset/distance instead and rebuilding the pose is what separates a polished follow from a janky one, and it is the same reason naive shoulder-swap teleports (reassigning the offset) while the pro version lerps the offset Vector3 then applies via PointToWorldSpace. This is a structural discipline, not a parameter: it determines whether smoothing can be FRAMERATE-INDEPENDENT and whether multiple smoothed channels (distance + offset + focus) can coexist. Grading 'smooth intermediates, derive the CFrame' keeps it discriminating from a build that lerps the output pose and inherits the jitter.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) the smoothed quantities are the focus/pivot, zoom distance, and/or shoulder-offset Vector3 (e.g. offset:Lerp(target, alpha) applied via PointToWorldSpace; focus smoothed then fed to CFrame.lookAt), AND (2) the final camera CFrame is rebuilt from those smoothed inputs (lookAt / fromMatrix / distance-along-look), NOT lerped directly toward a moving goal CFrame in the render step. Lerping the offset vector for a glide shoulder-swap and a clean lookAt/fromMatrix reconstruction are credited toward full marks. current.CFrame:Lerp(goalCFrame, alpha) toward a moving target does NOT satisfy this; smoothing some intermediates while still lerping the final follow CFrame earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Smooth the pivot/focus point, the zoom distance, and the shoulder-offset Vector3 — not the camera CFrame. Store cameraOffset as a Vector3 and lerp IT toward the target each frame, apply it via PointToWorldSpace, smooth the focus, then rebuild the pose with CFrame.lookAt(cameraPos, smoothedFocus) (or fromMatrix). Never write camera.CFrame = camera.CFrame:Lerp(goalCFrame, alpha) toward a moving target inside RenderStep.

grading.pass: Commits to smoothing intermediates and deriving the pose: (1) the smoothed quantities are the focus/pivot, zoom distance, and/or shoulder-offset Vector3 (offset:Lerp applied via PointToWorldSpace; focus smoothed then fed to CFrame.lookAt), AND (2) the final camera CFrame is rebuilt from those smoothed inputs via lookAt / fromMatrix / distance-along-look. Full marks add a glide shoulder-swap by lerping the offset VECTOR (not the CFrame) and a clean lookAt/fromMatrix reconstruction.
grading.partial: Smooths some intermediates (e.g. distance or FOV) but STILL lerps the final camera CFrame toward a moving goal for the follow itself, so the core follow inherits the jitter even though a side channel is smoothed correctly.
grading.fail: Lerps the final camera CFrame straight at a moving target every render frame (current.CFrame:Lerp(goalCFrame, alpha) inside RenderStep) — the classic jittery/desynced custom camera that fights the camera's own state — with no intermediate-smoothing-then-derive discipline.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — CONTEXT-DRIVEN CAMERA STATE MACHINE. The camera is a state machine of distinct, tuned MODES (e.g. explore/default-follow, sprint, aim-ADS, lock-on, mounted/vehicle, menu, cutscene) sharing ONE bind loop and ONE smoother, where each mode supplies its OWN FieldOfView, follow distance, shoulder/offset, and sensitivity as DATA, and a single dt-corrected smoother blends BETWEEN modes on transition so switching never pops. The discriminator is whether the build commits to per-context tuned modes with smoothed transitions, expressed as parameter-blending not CFrame-swapping: passing requires the build to state (1) at least THREE distinct gameplay modes each owning its own tuned FOV/distance/offset/sensitivity (one fixed default camera used in every context FAILS), AND (2) that mode changes are made by LERPING the PARAMETERS (offset Vector3, distance, FOV) toward the new mode's targets every frame through the shared smoother — so transitions glide — rather than teleporting/hard-cutting the camera CFrame between presets. A build with one fixed camera for all situations, or that hard-swaps CFrames between modes (instant ADS snap, instant shoulder flip), FAILS. A build that commits to >=3 parameter-driven modes blended on transition PASSES; a single render-step loop feeding all modes, ADS reduced-sensitivity, and a sprint pull-back+FOV widen push toward full marks. A build with multiple modes but instant (un-blended) transitions, or only two modes, earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: One fixed default camera used in every context is the generic baseline — the stock camera is a single mode with no transitions. The structural insight that elevates the whole category is one render-step loop + one smoother + modes-as-data: distance/offset/FOV/sensitivity are reusable channels every mode composes, so aiming, exploring, sprinting and cutscenes each feel right and switching reads as INTENTIONAL. The specific above-generic discipline is that a mode change must LERP the PARAMETERS between presets, not swap CFrames — the common amateur mistake is teleporting the camera (instant ADS snap, instant shoulder flip) because the code reassigns CFrames directly; storing each mode as {offset, distance, FOV, sensitivity} and interpolating the parameters means the SAME follow code produces all modes and every transition is automatically smooth. This directly mirrors the project's shared-system-module philosophy. Grading >=3 tuned modes + blended-parameter transitions keeps it discriminating: a multi-mode parameter-blended controller clears it; a single-default-camera or CFrame-swapping build cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) >=3 distinct gameplay modes (e.g. explore, sprint, aim-ADS, lock-on, vehicle, cutscene) EACH with its own tuned FieldOfView + follow distance + shoulder/offset + sensitivity, AND (2) transitions made by lerping the PARAMETERS (offset Vector3, distance, FOV) toward the new mode's targets through one shared dt-corrected smoother (glide, not teleport). A single render-step loop driving all modes, ADS reduced-sensitivity, and sprint pull-back+FOV are credited toward full marks. One fixed camera for every context, or hard CFrame-swaps between modes, does NOT satisfy this; multiple modes with un-blended instant transitions, or only two modes, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Build the camera as a state machine of modes sharing one BindToRenderStep loop and one smoother: store each mode (default-follow, sprint, aim-ADS, lock-on, vehicle, cutscene) as a small parameter set {offset, distance, FOV, sensitivity}. On a mode change, lerp the PARAMETERS toward the new mode's targets every frame (not the CFrame) so the same follow code produces all modes and transitions glide instead of popping.

grading.pass: Commits to per-context tuned modes blended via parameters: (1) >=3 distinct gameplay modes each owning its own tuned FieldOfView + follow distance + shoulder/offset + sensitivity, AND (2) mode changes made by lerping the PARAMETERS (offset Vector3, distance, FOV) toward the new mode's targets every frame through one shared smoother so transitions glide. Full marks add a single render-step loop feeding all modes, ADS reduced-sensitivity, and a sprint pull-back+FOV widen.
grading.partial: Multiple modes exist but transitions are instant/un-blended (parameters or CFrames hard-cut on switch), OR only TWO distinct modes are present rather than the required three. The mode concept is there but either the count or the blended-transition discipline is missing.
grading.fail: One fixed default camera used in every context (no modes), or modes that hard-swap CFrames between presets (instant ADS snap, instant shoulder flip) rather than lerping parameters through a shared smoother.

criteria.statement: DECOUPLE AIM/LOOK FROM THE SMOOTHED FOLLOW BODY — RIG-AGNOSTIC. The direction the camera AIMS is computed on a channel INDEPENDENT of the smoothed/sprung follow POSITION, so the camera tracks where the player (or a tracked target) is looking responsively while the body/position lags through its smoother — rather than orientation being merely 'whatever direction the lagged follow CFrame happens to face.' This is a third-person/OTS OR first-person concern; do NOT require first-person body-flatten mechanics. A PASS requires committing to the core decoupling fact (1): the LOOK/AIM orientation is driven by a SEPARATE channel from the follow-POSITION smoother — e.g. self-accumulated pitch/yaw, mouse/input-delta look, OR a tracked aim/look-target (such as a lock-on target) feeds the camera's orientation, while a critically-damped spring / dt-corrected smoother drives ONLY the follow position/pivot — so the aim is NOT inherited from the single lagged follow CFrame and does NOT drift behind the player on fast turns. A build whose camera orientation is simply the orientation of the smoothed follow CFrame (look and position share one lagged channel, so aim trails the player), or a pure stock default follow camera with no scripted aim channel at all, FAILS. A build that drives aim/look on a channel separate from the position smoother PASSES. Full marks ADD the offset-induced aim correction so the framing stays geometrically aligned at a non-zero offset: for an OTS/aim rig, aiming at a FAR focus down the look vector (PointToWorldSpace ~ -100000 -> CFrame.lookAt) so the shoulder offset doesn't cross the aim off-center (never lookAt the head with an OTS offset); for a first-person/body-driven rig, rebuilding the BODY from ONLY the camera's horizontal axis (Humanoid.AutoRotate=false; CFrame.fromMatrix from horizontal Right/Up, yaw-only never pitch/roll) with clamped pitch (~+/-45-75 deg) and asymmetric vertical sensitivity (delta.Y * ~0.4).
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The stock default follow camera couples look and position into one channel, so above-generic rigs must split them: aiming must read the player's (or target's) intent responsively — a sprung orientation lags the crosshair behind fast turns and feels mushy — while the position smooths separately. Inheriting orientation from the single lagged follow CFrame (so aim trails the player) is the exact decoupling mistake amateur and stock rigs make, and it is rig-agnostic: both an OTS spring rig (whose look-target/aim channel feeds orientation) and a first-person rig must solve it. The prior version additionally GATED the pass on the offset-aim-correction mechanics (far-focus magnitude / fromMatrix body rebuild), which an OTS artifact that genuinely decouples its look channel via a lock-on target need not spell out — so it must stay a full-marks discriminator, not a pass gate, or it collapses the separation between a real decoupled rig and a do-nothing stock camera.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing the camera's LOOK/AIM orientation comes from a channel SEPARATE from the follow-POSITION smoother — self-accumulated pitch/yaw, input-delta look, or a tracked aim/look-target (e.g. a lock-on target) feeding orientation while a spring/dt-corrected smoother drives ONLY the follow position/pivot (NOT orientation = the lagged follow CFrame's facing). The offset-aim correction is credited toward FULL MARKS: a FAR focus down the look vector (PointToWorldSpace ~ -100000 -> CFrame.lookAt) for an OTS/aim rig, OR Humanoid.AutoRotate=false + a torso rebuilt via CFrame.fromMatrix from only the camera's horizontal axis with clamped pitch and asymmetric vertical sensitivity for a first-person rig. Orientation taken straight from the smoothed follow CFrame, or a pure stock default follow camera with no scripted aim channel, does NOT satisfy this. A decoupled aim channel WITH the offset correction earns full marks; the decoupled aim channel alone is a clean pass.
criteria.concrete_fix: Drive aim/look orientation from a channel separate from the follow-position smoother: accumulate pitch/yaw yourself (or read a lock-on/aim target) to set the camera's orientation, and let the critically-damped spring / dt-corrected smoother move ONLY the follow position/pivot — never let orientation be inherited from the lagged follow CFrame. For full marks, correct the framing-offset aim error: for an OTS/aim rig, aim at a far focus = PointToWorldSpace(offX, offY, -100000) fed to CFrame.lookAt (never lookAt the head); for a first-person/body rig, set Humanoid.AutoRotate=false and rebuild the torso via CFrame.fromMatrix from only the camera's horizontal Right/Up vectors (yaw only) with pitch clamped ~+/-45-75 deg and reduced vertical sensitivity.

grading.pass: Commits to the core decoupling: aim/look orientation is driven by a channel SEPARATE from the follow-POSITION smoother — self-accumulated pitch/yaw, input-delta look, or a tracked aim/look-target (lock-on) feeds orientation while the spring/dt-corrected smoother drives only the follow position/pivot, so aim is NOT inherited from the single lagged follow CFrame. FULL MARKS additionally add the offset-induced aim correction: FAR-focus down the look vector (PointToWorldSpace ~ -100000 -> CFrame.lookAt) for an OTS/aim rig, OR a first-person body rebuild (Humanoid.AutoRotate=false; CFrame.fromMatrix from only the horizontal axis) with clamped pitch and asymmetric vertical sensitivity (delta.Y * ~0.4).
grading.partial: Gestures at a separate look/aim notion but it is ambiguous whether orientation is genuinely decoupled from the position smoother (e.g. names a look-target but also implies the lagged follow CFrame drives facing), OR provides only the offset-aim correction mechanics without clearly stating the aim channel is separate from the position smoother. The decoupling is implied but not committed.
grading.fail: Camera orientation is simply the orientation of the smoothed follow CFrame (look and position share one lagged channel, so aim drifts behind the player), OR a pure stock default follow camera with no scripted aim channel at all. No separate aim/look channel is committed.

criteria.change_reason: The prior (already once-revised) criterion required BOTH a decoupled aim channel AND the offset-induced aim correction (far-focus for OTS, or fromMatrix body rebuild for FP) for a pass. The GREAT artifact is an OTS spring rig with a lock-on/two-target look channel and a shoulder offset — it genuinely decouples aim (the lock-on target feeds orientation while the critically-damped spring drives only follow position) but its summary does not spell out the far-focus PointToWorldSpace magnitude, so the required prong (2) failed it, scoring identically to the do-nothing MEAN stock camera — zero discrimination, the exact defect being fixed. The rewrite makes the rig-agnostic core invariant (aim/look orientation on a channel SEPARATE from the position smoother — which a lock-on look-target plus a position-only spring satisfies) the sole pass gate, which the GREAT rig commits to and the stock coupled-channel MEAN camera does not. The offset-aim correction (far-focus / fromMatrix body rebuild) and asymmetric vertical sensitivity are preserved but moved to FULL MARKS so they still reward depth without nuking discrimination, and so first-person artifacts remain fully creditable.

criteria.statement: MOVEMENT-STATE-GATED FRAMING THAT EASES TO NEUTRAL — RIG-AGNOSTIC, DISTINCT FROM THE SMOOTHER'S OWN SETTLE. The camera changes its FRAMING in response to the subject's actual movement STATE/SPEED and eases that change back to neutral when the state clears — so motion reads as embodied rather than a fixed, unchanging follow. This is NOT first-person-only and is NOT the follow-smoother merely catching up: a single critically-damped spring settling its position when the target stops does NOT satisfy this, because that is the position smoother converging, not a movement-gated framing layer. A PASS requires committing to BOTH: (1) at least ONE framing channel whose TARGET is selected/scaled by a real movement STATE or clamped (preferably horizontal) SPEED — e.g. a sprint/dash state that pulls the follow distance back and/or widens FOV, a velocity-scaled walk-bob amplitude, a fall-speed landing dip, or a look-delta turn/lag sway — applied as an ADDITIVE offset over the base OR as a mode-PARAMETER (distance/FOV/shoulder-offset) shift, NOT a constant framing that is identical whether sprinting, walking, or idle; AND (2) that channel EASES IN AND OUT — the framing change is blended/lerped (eased transition, smoothed amplitude) toward its gated target and back to neutral when the gating state/speed drops, with NO hard snap-on/snap-off at the state boundary and NO frozen mid-cycle pose. A camera with ONE fixed framing for every movement state (same distance/FOV whether sprinting or standing still, no velocity-reactive layer), a framing change that HARD-CUTS the instant the state flips (instant sprint pull-back with no blend), or an additive aliveness layer that runs at constant amplitude regardless of motion, FAILS. A build that gates a framing channel on real movement state/speed AND eases it in and out PASSES; a SECOND independently-gated channel (e.g. sprint pull-back PLUS a velocity-scaled bob/turn-sway), a non-linear gate curve, and a named onset/release smoothing constant push toward full marks. (A first-person rig satisfies prong (1) with velocity-scaled head-bob/breathing/turn-sway eased to zero; a third-person/OTS rig satisfies it equally with a sprint/dash-state pull-back+FOV-widen entered and left via eased mode transitions — the discriminator is the movement-GATE + ease-in/out + over-the-base/parameter application, not the rig and not a particular bob effect.)
criteria.above_generic_rationale: A follow that frames the subject identically whether they are sprinting, walking, or standing still reads as inert in BOTH first- and third-person; the embodied, above-generic move is to let the FRAMING react to the actual movement state and ease that reaction in and out — a sprint pull-back+FOV-widen that glides in on a real sprint and glides back out, or a velocity-scaled bob/turn-sway that eases to zero on stop. The non-obvious quality details are exactly what separates this from both the stock camera and from a naive bolt-on: the change must be GATED on real movement (so it can't fire idle and scales with speed), it must EASE IN AND OUT at the state boundary (a hard sprint-distance snap pops; a constant bob strobes), and it must be layered over the base or driven as a smoothed mode parameter rather than baked into one fixed pose. Critically, it must be distinguished from the follow spring merely settling when the target stops — that settle is the position smoother converging (its own criterion), not a movement-gated framing layer, and a build that only settles still feels like a single static framing. Keying the criterion to movement-GATE + ease-in/out + over-the-base/parameter application, rather than to a specific first-person head-bob, makes it discriminate the polished rig of either genre (sprint-mode eased pull-back, or eased velocity bob) from a stock fixed-framing follow — and from a build whose only 'reactivity' is the smoother catching up.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) >=1 framing channel whose target is selected/scaled by a real movement STATE or clamped (preferably horizontal) SPEED — a sprint/dash state pulling distance back and/or widening FOV, a velocity-scaled walk-bob amplitude, a fall-speed landing dip, or a look-delta turn/lag sway — applied as an ADDITIVE offset over the base (Humanoid.CameraOffset or base * offsetCFrame) OR as a movement-gated mode PARAMETER shift (distance/FOV/shoulder-offset), NOT a constant framing identical across movement states; AND (2) that the framing change EASES IN AND OUT — blended/lerped toward its gated target and back to neutral when the state/speed drops (eased mode transition or smoothed amplitude), with no hard snap-on/off and no frozen mid-cycle pose. EXPLICITLY NOT sufficient: the follow position smoother simply settling when the target stops (that is the spring converging, not a movement-gated framing layer — graded under the look-ahead criterion). A second independently-gated channel (sprint pull-back PLUS a velocity-scaled bob/turn-sway), a non-linear gate curve, and a named onset/release smoothing constant are credited toward full marks. One fixed framing for all movement states, a hard-cut framing change at the state boundary, or a constant-amplitude additive layer does NOT satisfy this; a movement-gated framing channel WITHOUT ease-in/out (snaps), or an eased channel that is NOT actually gated on movement state/speed, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Add at least one framing channel gated on real movement state/speed and ease it in and out. Third-person/OTS: give sprint/dash its own tuned {distance, FOV} (pull the follow back + widen FOV) and lerp the PARAMETERS toward it (and back to the explore neutral) through your shared smoother when the sprint state toggles on actual horizontal MoveDirection — a glide, not a snap. Or first-person: drive a velocity-scaled walk-bob / turn-sway as an additive Humanoid.CameraOffset whose amplitude lerps toward a speed-proportional target and eases to zero on stop. Either way the channel must (a) read ACTUAL movement (not run constantly) and (b) ease in AND out at the state boundary. Do NOT rely on the follow spring's own settle-on-stop to satisfy this — that is the position smoother converging, not a movement-gated framing layer.

grading.pass: Commits to BOTH: (1) >=1 framing channel whose target is selected/scaled by real movement STATE or clamped (preferably horizontal) SPEED — sprint/dash pull-back+FOV-widen, velocity-scaled walk-bob, fall-speed landing dip, or look-delta turn/lag sway — applied as an additive offset over the base OR a movement-gated mode parameter (distance/FOV/shoulder-offset) shift, not a constant framing across all movement states, AND (2) that channel eases IN AND OUT (blended/lerped toward the gated target and back to neutral when the state/speed clears), with no hard snap-on/off and no frozen mid-cycle pose. The follow smoother's own settle-on-stop does NOT count toward either prong. Full marks add a second independently-gated channel (sprint pull-back PLUS a velocity-scaled bob/turn-sway), a non-linear gate curve, and a named onset/release smoothing constant.
grading.partial: Has a movement-state/speed-gated framing channel but it HARD-CUTS at the state boundary (instant sprint pull-back / instant bob on/off, no eased in/out), OR has an eased additive/parameter framing layer that is NOT actually gated on real movement state/speed (runs at constant amplitude or blends on a non-movement trigger). One of the two core facts present, the other missing.
grading.fail: One fixed framing for every movement state (same distance/FOV/offset whether sprinting, walking, or idle; no velocity-reactive framing channel at all — the stock default follow with a constant FOV), OR the ONLY motion reactivity is the follow position smoother settling when the target stops (the spring converging, not a movement-gated framing layer), OR an additive aliveness layer that runs at constant amplitude regardless of motion. A pure stock default follow camera fails here.

criteria.change_reason: The prior criterion (already once-revised) demanded a velocity-GATED *additive aliveness layer* specifically of the walk-bob / landing-dip / turn-sway family that eases its AMPLITUDE to zero. The GREAT artifact is a third-person/OTS spring rig that ships no head-bob/breathing/turn-sway at all — its movement reactivity lives in a sprint/dash MODE (pull-back + FOV widen) entered via eased transitions, plus reactive FOV. So the old wording made GREAT FAIL identically to the do-nothing MEAN stock camera (fixed FOV 70, one camera in every context) — zero discrimination, the exact defect being fixed. The rewrite keeps the SAME underlying systems-depth invariant (camera framing reacts to ACTUAL movement state/speed and eases back to neutral, applied over the base or as a mode parameter rather than baked-in) but broadens prong (1) to credit a movement-state-gated framing PARAMETER shift (sprint pull-back + FOV widen via eased mode transitions) as an equal path alongside the FP bob family — which the GREAT rig demonstrably commits to ('a sprint mode with tuned FOV/distance and smoothed transitions' + 'reactive FOV kicks (sprint/dash)'). Crucially it ADDS an explicit carve-out that the follow-smoother's own settle-on-stop does NOT count, so the GREAT rig must pass via its genuine movement-gated, eased sprint-framing channel rather than via the spring settle (which is graded under the look-ahead criterion), and so a build that only has a settling spring still fails. Net: GREAT now PASSES (sprint-state-gated eased pull-back/FOV widen over the base), while the MEAN stock follow — fixed framing for all movement states, no eased transitions, no velocity-reactive layer — still FAILS both prongs. First-person artifacts remain fully creditable via the preserved bob/sway path.

criteria.statement: DIRECTIONAL IMPULSE KICK — DISTINCT FROM OMNIDIRECTIONAL SHAKE. A discrete DIRECTIONAL kick (recoil up, hit-from-the-left, landing) is applied to the look on top of normal follow and decays back via spring/damping, conveying WHERE force came from — separate from the omnidirectional trauma rumble. The discriminator is whether the build commits to a directional, spring-returning impulse that is architecturally distinct from the noise shake: passing requires (1) a directional impulse with a DIRECTION tied to the event (recoil pitches the look up, a hit from the left yaws it left, a landing dips it) — not an omnidirectional random offset — AND (2) a spring/damped return that springs the look back home after the kick (decays, optionally overshoots and settles), layered ADDITIVELY over the follow. A build that only has omnidirectional shake (rumble with no direction), or a kick that hard-snaps back with no spring return, FAILS. A build that commits to a directional impulse with a spring-damped return, layered over the follow PASSES; combining the directional kick WITH the trauma shake (rumble + direction together, the modern game-feel pattern) and an event-typed preset set (recoil vs landing vs hit-react) push toward full marks. A build that gestures at a kick but applies it omnidirectionally (indistinguishable from shake), or with no spring return, earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: A trauma/noise shake conveys RUMBLE but not DIRECTION — it can't tell the player a hit came from the left or that recoil pushed up. A discrete directional kick that springs back conveys exactly that: recoil up, hit-from-the-left, a landing dip — and layering the directional impulse WITH the omnidirectional trauma shake is the pattern modern game-feel toolkits (hit-stop + camera impulse) bundle, which is what makes hits feel grounded 'rather than scripted.' The above-generic details are that the impulse must carry a real DIRECTION tied to the event (not be omnidirectional, or it's just shake by another name) and must decay via a spring/damped return (not hard-snap home), applied additively over the follow so it composes. This is distinct from the trauma-shake criterion: a build can have an excellent omnidirectional trauma shake and still lack any directional impulse. Grading directional-impulse + spring-return + additive-over-follow keeps it discriminating from a shake-only or snap-back build.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) a directional impulse whose DIRECTION is tied to the event (recoil up, hit-from-the-left yaw, landing dip) — not an omnidirectional random offset — AND (2) a spring/damped return that brings the look back home (decay, optional overshoot/settle), layered additively over the follow. Combining the directional kick with the trauma shake (rumble + direction) and event-typed presets (recoil/landing/hit-react) are credited toward full marks. Omnidirectional shake only, or a kick that hard-snaps back with no spring, does NOT satisfy this; a kick applied omnidirectionally (indistinguishable from shake) or with no spring return earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Add a directional impulse separate from the omnidirectional shake: on recoil pitch the look up, on a hit-from-the-left yaw it left, on landing dip it — each a discrete kick with a DIRECTION tied to the event — then let a spring/damper return the look home (decay, slight overshoot, settle). Apply it additively on top of the follow and combine it with the trauma shake so impacts carry both rumble and direction.

grading.pass: Commits to a directional, spring-returning impulse architecturally distinct from the noise shake: (1) a directional impulse whose DIRECTION is tied to the event (recoil up, hit-from-the-left yaw, landing dip) — not omnidirectional random — AND (2) a spring/damped return that brings the look home (decay, optional overshoot/settle), layered additively over the follow. Full marks add combining the directional kick WITH the trauma shake and an event-typed preset set (recoil vs landing vs hit-react).
grading.partial: Gestures at a kick but applies it omnidirectionally (indistinguishable from the trauma shake), OR has a clearly directional kick but it hard-snaps back home with no spring/damped return.
grading.fail: Only omnidirectional shake (rumble with no direction) is present, with no discrete directional impulse at all — or a directional kick that both lacks direction-per-event AND hard-snaps back.

criteria.statement: PARAMETERIZED RIG WITH AXIS-ASYMMETRIC SMOOTHING. The camera pose is built from named tunables (distance, height-offset, lateral shoulder-offset, look-target) rather than magic numbers, and smoothing constants are tuned PER AXIS and PER DIRECTION rather than one uniform damping for everything. The discriminator is whether the build commits to both generalization and perception-aware asymmetric tuning: passing requires (1) the camera position derived as distance + height-offset + lateral-offset + look-target exposed as named knobs (so the SAME rig becomes OTS/isometric/top-down/side-scroller by changing constants, not by rewriting), NOT a hardcoded fixed feel; AND (2) asymmetric smoothing constants — different damping for HORIZONTAL vs VERTICAL motion, and/or for moving-up vs moving-down / zoom-in vs zoom-out (an asymmetric, perception-aware response) — rather than a single uniform smoothing alpha applied to all axes and directions. A build with hardcoded magic-number positioning and one uniform smoothing constant FAILS. A build that parameterizes the rig AND tunes smoothing asymmetrically by axis/direction PASSES; the explicit perception rationale (players perceive vertical and horizontal motion differently) and exposing the smoothing as named knobs push toward full marks. A build that parameterizes the rig but uses uniform smoothing (or asymmetric smoothing on a hardcoded rig) earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The stock camera gives exactly one feel (centered, fixed zoom curve). Parameterizing position as distance + height-offset + lateral-offset + look-target is the 'generalize, don't hardcode' move that lets the SAME rig become side-scroller, isometric, over-the-shoulder or top-down by changing constants instead of forking the code — and it's the precondition for the mode state machine to drive those parameters per context. On the smoothing side, Eiserloh's perception result is that players perceive vertical and horizontal motion DIFFERENTLY, so a single uniform damping ignores directional perception bias; tuning axes (and directions: moving-up vs down, zoom-in vs out) independently lets the camera feel tight where it must and loose where it should — a hand-tuned, perception-aware nicety that generic uniform damping never captures. Grading parameterized-rig + axis/direction-asymmetric-smoothing keeps it discriminating from a magic-number, uniform-damping build.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) camera position derived from named tunables — distance + height-offset + lateral shoulder-offset + look-target — (so the rig generalizes to OTS/isometric/top-down by changing constants), NOT hardcoded magic numbers, AND (2) asymmetric smoothing: different damping constants for horizontal vs vertical, and/or moving-up vs down / zoom-in vs zoom-out, rather than one uniform alpha for all axes/directions. The explicit perception rationale and exposing smoothing as named knobs are credited toward full marks. Hardcoded positioning with one uniform smoothing constant does NOT satisfy this; a parameterized rig with uniform smoothing (or asymmetric smoothing on a hardcoded rig) earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Expose the camera pose as named tunables — distance, height-offset, lateral shoulder-offset, and a look-target — and derive position from them (so changing constants turns the same rig into OTS, isometric, top-down or side-scroller) instead of hardcoding magic numbers. Then give smoothing asymmetric constants: separate damping for horizontal vs vertical motion, and for zoom-in vs zoom-out / up vs down, since players perceive those axes differently — not one uniform alpha everywhere.

grading.pass: Commits to both generalization and perception-aware asymmetric tuning: (1) camera position derived from named tunables — distance + height-offset + lateral shoulder-offset + look-target — so the same rig generalizes to OTS/isometric/top-down by changing constants, AND (2) asymmetric smoothing constants (different damping for horizontal vs vertical, and/or up vs down / zoom-in vs zoom-out). Full marks add the explicit perception rationale and exposing the smoothing itself as named knobs.
grading.partial: Parameterizes the rig from named tunables but uses one uniform smoothing constant for all axes/directions, OR tunes smoothing asymmetrically by axis/direction but on a hardcoded magic-number rig. One of the two halves present, the other missing.
grading.fail: Hardcoded magic-number positioning AND a single uniform smoothing constant applied to all axes and directions — neither generalization nor perception-aware asymmetric tuning.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — FRAMERATE-INDEPENDENT SPRING FOLLOW WITH LOOK-AHEAD. The focus/position is driven by a critically-damped SPRING (or dt-corrected exponential damping) — not a rigid CFrame lock and not a fixed-alpha lerp — with FRAMERATE-INDEPENDENT smoothing AND velocity-based look-ahead/lead so fast movement reveals what is ahead and the camera settles when the target stops. The discriminator is whether the build commits to BOTH dt-correct smoothing AND lead-with-settle: passing requires the build to state (1) framerate-independent smoothing by a concrete mechanism — alpha = 1 - f^dt (e.g. f=0.25), equivalently 1 - math.exp(-k*dt), OR a real damped-spring integrator with a damping ratio (critically-damped ~ no overshoot) — explicitly NOT a constant per-frame alpha like cam:Lerp(goal, 0.2); AND (2) velocity-based look-ahead/lead (the focus leads the target's motion so fast movement shows what's ahead) that settles back when the target stops. A build using a rigid CFrame lock, or a naive fixed-alpha lerp with no dt term (faster/floatier on different hardware, never overshoots/settles), FAILS. A build that commits to dt-corrected spring/exponential smoothing AND velocity look-ahead-with-settle PASSES; sampling a physics target on RunService.Stepped (not RenderStepped) when the subject is physically simulated, frame-delta averaging to ride FPS spikes, and a SnapToCriticalDamping-tuned settle push toward full marks. A build with dt-correct smoothing but no look-ahead (or look-ahead on a framerate-dependent lerp) earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The single biggest tell of an amateur camera: cam = cam:Lerp(goal, 0.2) every frame with no dt term moves a different fraction at 30 vs 144/240 FPS, so it's silky on the dev's machine and stiff/floaty everywhere else, jitters with FPS-unlockers, and can NEVER produce the subtle overshoot-and-settle that reads as AAA. The default Roblox camera is already framerate-correct, so a custom rig only matches it by doing dt-corrected smoothing — the exp(-k*dt) identity (which stays bounded, unlike alpha*dt which can exceed 1 and break the lerp) and the spring integrator are the concrete copy-able formulas. A plain continuous lerp always reads as a 'catch-up' trail where the camera FOLLOWS rather than LEADS; a tuned spring gives genuine mass and resistance, and velocity-based look-ahead makes the camera lead the action and reveal what's ahead, settling when motion stops. The non-obvious mastery layer — sampling a physics-driven target on Stepped (in sync with the physics pipeline) rather than RenderStepped (which runs BEFORE physics and reads a half-stepped target) — is the root-cause fix for the 'spring camera on a car is jittery no matter the damper' complaint, where generic advice only says 'lower the damper' (hides, not fixes). Grading dt-correct-spring + look-ahead-with-settle is exactly the systems-depth-not-surface bar.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) framerate-independent smoothing by a concrete mechanism — alpha = 1 - f^dt, or 1 - math.exp(-k*dt), or a damped-spring integrator with a damping ratio — explicitly NOT a constant per-frame alpha (cam:Lerp(goal, 0.2)); AND (2) velocity-based look-ahead/lead that reveals what's ahead during fast motion and settles when the target stops. Sampling a physics subject on RunService.Stepped (not RenderStepped), frame-delta averaging, and a critically-damped settle are credited toward full marks. A rigid CFrame lock, or a naive fixed-alpha lerp with no dt term, does NOT satisfy this; dt-correct smoothing without look-ahead (or look-ahead on a framerate-dependent lerp) earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Replace cam:Lerp(goal, 0.2) with framerate-independent smoothing: alpha = 1 - math.exp(-decay * dt) (dt from the render step), or a real damped-spring integrator tuned near critical damping for a weighty settle without overshoot. Add velocity-based look-ahead so the focus LEADS the target's motion (revealing what's ahead) and eases back when it stops. If the subject is physics-driven (vehicle/ragdoll), sample its position on RunService.Stepped instead of RenderStepped so the spring reads a settled target.

grading.pass: Commits to BOTH dt-correct smoothing AND lead-with-settle: (1) framerate-independent smoothing by a concrete mechanism — alpha = 1 - f^dt, or 1 - math.exp(-k*dt), or a damped-spring integrator with a damping ratio — explicitly NOT a constant per-frame alpha, AND (2) velocity-based look-ahead/lead that reveals what's ahead during fast motion and settles when the target stops. Full marks add sampling a physics subject on RunService.Stepped (not RenderStepped), frame-delta averaging, and a critically-damped settle.
grading.partial: dt-correct spring/exponential smoothing is present but there is NO velocity look-ahead, OR look-ahead is present but bolted onto a framerate-dependent fixed-alpha lerp. One of the two required commitments present, the other missing.
grading.fail: Uses a rigid CFrame lock, or a naive fixed-alpha lerp with no dt term (cam:Lerp(goal, 0.2)) that runs faster/floatier on different hardware and never overshoots/settles — no framerate-independent mechanism and no lead-with-settle.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — REACTIVE FOV + ADDITIVE TRAUMA SHAKE. Dynamic FieldOfView kicks on gameplay state (sprint/dash/speed/ADS) AND a layered ADDITIVE trauma/impulse screen-shake — a decaying trauma scalar driving smoothed-noise rotational+positional offset composited OVER the follow CFrame — fires on gameplay events (impacts, landings, explosions, recoil). The discriminator is whether the build commits to BOTH a context-tied tweened FOV AND a trauma-model shake that decays and LAYERS over the base: passing requires (1) FieldOfView TWEENED (not snapped) toward a target tied to a gameplay CONTEXT — widen on sprint/dash to sell speed, narrow for ADS/scope — gated on actual state (e.g. MoveDirection.Magnitude>0, or horizontal-velocity-only so jumping doesn't spike FOV), with a base/min/max band; AND (2) a trauma model: a normalized trauma in [0,1] that EVENTS add to and that decays over time, with shake amplitude = trauma^2 (or ^3) so footsteps and explosions are perceptually distinct, driven by smoothed/Perlin noise (not per-frame math.random) applied as a ROTATIONAL-primary CFrame offset composited over the follow (camera.CFrame = base * shakeCFrame), with fade-in/out. A constant FOV, a snapped FOV, raw-velocity FOV that spikes on jumps, per-frame random jitter, or shake that overwrites/fights the follow FAILS. A build that commits to tweened-context-FOV AND a trauma^2 noise shake that decays and layers PASSES; rotational-over-translational shake (translation is nausea-inducing in 3D), magnitude+roughness+fade-envelope parameterization, sustained-vs-one-shot presets, and distance-attenuation push toward full marks. A build with reactive FOV but a non-trauma flat shake (or trauma shake but constant/snapped FOV) earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: Stock FOV is a fixed 70 forever and conveys nothing; the brain reads a widening FOV as acceleration even at constant speed, so reactive FOV is a core juice channel — but only if it's TWEENED (not snapped) and tied to a CONTEXT (sprint/ADS) and gated so it can't be cheesed idle or spiked by jumps (mask out vertical velocity). On the shake side, the generic version is cam.CFrame *= CFrame.Angles(random, random, random) — uncorrelated jitter that strobes, reads cheap, fights the player's aim and pops on/off. The trauma model (Eiserloh) is the well-known game-feel result: squaring/cubing a decaying trauma scalar gives a nonlinear impact hierarchy (0.3 trauma -> ~3% shake, 0.9 -> ~73%) so the SAME system makes a footstep and an explosion feel different automatically; Perlin/smoothed noise gives coherent, continuous, replayable motion (survives slow-mo) instead of strobing; rotational-primary shake conveys impact while keeping the world readable (3D translational shake is 'super lame', disorienting, bad in VR); and applying it as base * shakeCFrame with fade envelopes COMPOSES over the follow instead of stomping it. Grading reactive-context-FOV AND trauma^2-noise-shake-that-layers keeps it discriminating: a constant-FOV + random-jitter build fails, a context-tweened-FOV + decaying-trauma-noise-over-base build clears it.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) FieldOfView TWEENED toward a context-tied target (sprint/dash widen, ADS narrow), gated on real movement state (MoveDirection.Magnitude>0, or horizontal-velocity-only so jumps don't spike it) with a base/min/max band; AND (2) a trauma model — normalized trauma in [0,1] that events ADD to and that decays, amplitude = trauma^2/^3, driven by smoothed/Perlin noise (not per-frame random), applied as a rotational-primary CFrame offset composited over the follow (base * shakeCFrame) with fade-in/out. Rotational-over-translational shake, magnitude+roughness+fade-envelope params, sustained-vs-one-shot presets, and distance-attenuation are credited toward full marks. Constant/snapped FOV, raw-velocity FOV, per-frame random jitter, or shake that overwrites the follow does NOT satisfy this; reactive FOV with a flat non-trauma shake (or trauma shake with constant FOV) earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Tween Camera.FieldOfView (TweenService, Sine/Quad, ~0.2-0.4s) toward a context target — widen on sprint/dash (gate on horizontal MoveDirection so jumps and idle don't trigger it), narrow for ADS — and tween back to a base FOV on release. For shake, keep a trauma scalar in [0,1]: events add to it (small for footsteps, large for explosions, clamped), decay it each frame, and drive shake = trauma^2 through Perlin noise as a primarily ROTATIONAL CFrame offset multiplied onto the base (camera.CFrame = base * shakeCFrame) with fade-in/out — never per-frame math.random and never overwriting the follow.

grading.pass: Commits to BOTH a context-tied tweened FOV AND a trauma-model shake that decays and layers: (1) FieldOfView tweened (not snapped) toward a context-tied target (sprint/dash widen, ADS narrow), gated on real movement state (MoveDirection.Magnitude>0 or horizontal-velocity-only) with a base/min/max band, AND (2) a normalized trauma in [0,1] that events add to and that decays, amplitude = trauma^2/^3, driven by smoothed/Perlin noise, applied as a rotational-primary CFrame offset composited over the follow (base * shakeCFrame) with fade-in/out. Full marks add rotational-over-translational shake, magnitude+roughness+fade-envelope params, sustained-vs-one-shot presets, and distance-attenuation.
grading.partial: Has reactive context-tied FOV but the shake is a flat non-trauma effect (no decaying trauma scalar / no nonlinear amplitude), OR has a genuine decaying-trauma noise shake but the FOV is constant/snapped rather than tweened-and-context-tied. One channel correct, the other missing or generic.
grading.fail: Constant FOV, a snapped FOV, or raw-velocity FOV that spikes on jumps; AND/OR per-frame math.random jitter or shake that overwrites/fights the follow. No tweened-context FOV and no decaying trauma-model noise shake composited over the base.

criteria.statement: MULTIPLE REACTIVE CHANNELS, GAMEPLAY-DRIVEN, COMPOSITED OVER ONE BASE — NOT A SINGLE GIMMICK. High-speed / high-impact game feel is built from a STACK of distinct reactive channels, each driven by gameplay state/events and each composited over the SAME shared base follow/pose, rather than the camera shipping one lone reactive effect (just an FOV bump, just a shake) or none at all. The discriminator is whether the build commits to a genuine multi-channel reactive stack that coexists over one base: passing requires the build to state (1) at least THREE distinct reactive channels — drawn from reactive FOV kicks, a trauma/impact screen-shake, a collision/distance pull-in, a directional impulse kick, motion blur, chromatic/post — that are each tied to gameplay (a speed/sprint/dash state, an aim/ADS state, or an impact/landing/recoil event), AND (2) that these channels are applied so they COEXIST over the same base camera (additive offsets and/or smoothed mode parameters layered on the one follow/spring pose, each independently tunable/removable), NOT a single hard-written effect that owns the frame alone. A camera that ships exactly one reactive effect and calls it intensity, or zero reactive effects (the stock fixed-FOV follow), FAILS. A build that commits to >=3 gameplay-driven reactive channels coexisting over one shared base PASSES. Full marks ADD the tightest coordination layer: >=3 of those channels FIRING TOGETHER on a SHARED speed/impact threshold (speed crosses X -> FOV widen + speed-scaled shake + distance pull-back + motion blur all ramp; impact -> all kick) with shared non-linear ramp curves and a coordinated ramp-down when the state ends, rather than each channel merely co-existing on its own independent trigger.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The stated insight from the vehicle-camera intensity work is that felt intensity 'comes from combining multiple elements working simultaneously — not individual effects alone.' A single effect (just an FOV bump, just a shake) reads as a gimmick; the layered composition of FOV + speed shake + distance pull-back + motion blur is what makes a high-speed boost or heavy impact feel cinematic. The earlier version made the strict 'all >=3 fire on ONE shared threshold, coordinated as a stack' the pass gate — a real but rarely-summary-stated detail. A rig with three genuinely-built reactive channels (reactive FOV, trauma shake, collision pull-in) that each react to gameplay and compose over its shared spring base demonstrably has the systems-depth this criterion is about, yet it failed identically to a stock camera with ZERO reactive channels — zero discrimination, the exact defect being fixed. Keying the pass to '>=3 gameplay-driven channels coexisting over one base' (the buildable, observable invariant) while reserving 'all co-fire on a shared threshold' for full marks restores the separation: a multi-channel reactive rig clears it, a single-gimmick or stock build cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) >=3 distinct reactive channels (from: reactive FOV kicks, trauma/impact shake, collision/distance pull-in, directional impulse kick, motion blur, chromatic/post) each tied to gameplay state/events (a speed/sprint/dash state, an aim/ADS state, or an impact/landing/recoil event), AND (2) that they are applied as additive offsets and/or smoothed mode parameters layered over the SAME base follow/spring pose so they coexist (not one hard-written effect owning the frame alone). The tightest coordination — >=3 channels FIRING TOGETHER on a SHARED speed/impact threshold with shared ramp curves and a coordinated ramp-down — is credited toward FULL MARKS. Shipping exactly one reactive effect, or zero (stock fixed-FOV follow), does NOT satisfy this; two reactive channels, or three that do not clearly compose over a shared base, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Build at least three reactive channels and compose them over one base instead of shipping a single gimmick: e.g. reactive FOV kicks on sprint/dash/ADS, a trauma/impact screen-shake on hits/landings, and a collision/distance pull-in — each driven by gameplay state/events and each layered as an additive offset or smoothed mode parameter over the SAME follow/spring pose (independently tunable). For full marks, also drive several of them off ONE shared speed/impact threshold (speed crosses X -> FOV widen + speed-scaled shake + distance pull-back + motion blur all ramp together; impact -> all kick) and ramp them back down together when the state ends.

grading.pass: Commits to a genuine multi-channel reactive stack over one base: (1) >=3 distinct reactive channels (reactive FOV, trauma/impact shake, collision/distance pull-in, directional impulse, motion blur, chromatic/post) each tied to gameplay state/events, AND (2) applied as additive offsets and/or smoothed mode parameters composited over the SAME base follow/spring pose so they coexist (not one hard-written effect owning the frame). FULL MARKS additionally have >=3 of those channels FIRING TOGETHER on a SHARED speed/impact threshold with shared non-linear ramp curves and a coordinated ramp-down.
grading.partial: Only TWO reactive channels are present, OR three-plus reactive effects are named but it is not clear they compose over a shared base (they may overwrite the frame / be scattered one-offs rather than layered offsets/parameters over one follow pose).
grading.fail: Ships exactly one reactive effect (FOV alone, or shake alone) and calls it intensity, OR zero reactive effects at all (the stock fixed-FOV follow). No multi-channel reactive stack composited over a shared base.

criteria.change_reason: The old criterion required all >=3 reactive channels to FIRE TOGETHER on a single SHARED threshold, coordinated as one stack, for a pass. The GREAT artifact has three genuinely-built, gameplay-driven reactive channels (reactive FOV kicks, a trauma-based additive shake fired by events, and a collision raycast pull-in) all compositing over its shared critically-damped spring base, but it describes them as separate systems and never states they co-fire on one shared trigger — so it FAILED, identically to the MEAN stock camera that ships ZERO reactive effects. Zero discrimination, the exact defect being fixed. The rewrite makes the buildable, observable systems-depth invariant the GREAT rig actually commits to — >=3 distinct gameplay-driven reactive channels coexisting as additive offsets / smoothed parameters over ONE shared base — the pass bar, which the MEAN zero-effect stock follow cannot meet. The strict 'all co-fire on a shared single threshold with coordinated ramp-up/down' is preserved as the FULL-MARKS coordination layer, so the criterion still rewards the tightest stacking without nuking discrimination.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — COLLISION- AND OCCLUSION-AWARE FRAMING. The camera never clips through geometry or hides the subject: it raycasts from the target/focus toward the desired camera position to pull IN on obstruction and smoothly return when clear (Popper-style), AND handles TARGET occlusion (dolly/peek/fade when the player is blocked), with a smooth over-the-shoulder offset and side-swap near walls. The discriminator is whether the build commits to active occlusion handling with the correct gotchas: passing requires (1) a per-frame raycast/spherecast from focus to the ideal camera position (RaycastParams filtering the character AND its accessories/hats AND cloned projectiles — otherwise the avatar/projectiles register as 'obscuring' and the camera fights itself) that shortens distance to the hit with a small skin offset so it never clips through walls, OR an explicit engine-helper path (Camera:GetPartsObscuringTarget / GetLargestCutoffDistance, or DevCameraOcclusionMode=Invisicam to fade occluders) WITH the noted caveats (those helpers ignore Terrain, CanCollide=false, and Transparency>0.95); AND (2) an ASYMMETRIC response — snap IN instantly on obstruction (prevents a momentary clip-through) but smoothly lerp OUT when unobstructed (prevents a rubber-bandy pop). A custom Scriptable camera with NO occlusion handling (clips straight through walls — instantly amateur, and a regression below the stock camera's free PopperCam), or a symmetric lerp both ways, FAILS. A build that re-implements occlusion via filtered raycast + skin-offset + asymmetric snap-in/ease-out PASSES; a smooth over-the-shoulder offset with side-swap near walls, the GetPartsObscuringTarget ignore-list gotcha called out by name, and target dolly/peek/fade push toward full marks. A build that relies only on the stock Popper with no aim/OTS offset, or raycasts without filtering the character (so it fights itself), earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: Stock Roblox does Zoom/PopperCam occlusion for free, but a custom Scriptable camera LOSES it — so a hand-rolled rig with no occlusion clips straight through geometry and shows the backside of walls, the most immediately obvious mark of an unfinished camera AND a regression below the default. Re-implementing it is therefore required just to not regress, and the above-generic version (filtered raycast from focus to the ideal eye position, shorten to the hit with a skin offset, smooth recover) also enables tight over-the-shoulder framing the default can't do. The non-obvious gotchas are exactly the edge-case knowledge a rubric should encode: the character's own hats/accessories and cloned projectiles obscure the target EVERY frame unless filtered out (the camera yanks otherwise); GetPartsObscuringTarget silently skips Terrain, non-colliding parts and Transparency>0.95; and the obstruction response must be ASYMMETRIC — instant snap-in to avoid a one-frame clip, smooth ease-out to avoid a jarring pop (a symmetric lerp either clips or feels rubber-bandy). Knowing WHEN to ride the stock camera (Invisicam fade vs Popper zoom-in) is a genre choice. Grading filtered-raycast + asymmetric-response keeps it discriminating from a clip-through build or a naive symmetric lerp.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) a per-frame raycast/spherecast from focus to the ideal camera position with RaycastParams filtering the character + accessories/hats + cloned projectiles, shortening distance to the hit with a skin offset (OR an engine-helper path: GetPartsObscuringTarget/GetLargestCutoffDistance or DevCameraOcclusionMode=Invisicam, with the Terrain/non-collide/Transparency>0.95 caveats noted), AND (2) an ASYMMETRIC response — snap IN instantly on obstruction, smoothly ease OUT when clear. A smooth OTS offset with wall-side-swap, the accessory/projectile ignore-list gotcha named, and target dolly/peek/fade are credited toward full marks. No occlusion handling (clips through walls), or a symmetric lerp both ways, does NOT satisfy this; stock-Popper-only with no OTS offset, or an unfiltered raycast that fights the character, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Raycast (or spherecast) from the focus to the desired camera position every frame, with RaycastParams that filter out the character, its accessories/hats, AND any cloned projectiles, then clamp the camera to the hit point minus a small skin offset so it never clips through walls. Make the response asymmetric: snap IN instantly on obstruction, but smoothly lerp the distance back OUT once clear. For the stock path, pick DevCameraOcclusionMode=Invisicam (fade occluders) vs Zoom (pull in) by genre, and remember GetPartsObscuringTarget ignores Terrain, CanCollide=false parts, and Transparency>0.95.

grading.pass: Commits to active occlusion handling with the correct gotchas: (1) a per-frame raycast/spherecast from focus to the ideal camera position with RaycastParams filtering the character + accessories/hats + cloned projectiles, shortening to the hit with a skin offset (or an explicit engine-helper path — GetPartsObscuringTarget/GetLargestCutoffDistance or DevCameraOcclusionMode=Invisicam — with the Terrain/non-collide/Transparency>0.95 caveats noted), AND (2) an ASYMMETRIC response: snap IN instantly on obstruction, smoothly ease OUT when clear. Full marks add a smooth OTS offset with wall-side-swap, the accessory/projectile ignore-list gotcha named, and target dolly/peek/fade.
grading.partial: Relies only on the stock Popper with no aim/OTS offset (so it doesn't regress but adds nothing above default), OR raycasts but does NOT filter the character/accessories/projectiles (so the camera fights itself), OR uses a symmetric in/out response that is at least present but either clips or feels rubber-bandy.
grading.fail: A custom Scriptable camera with NO occlusion handling at all — clips straight through walls and shows the backside of geometry (instantly amateur, a regression below the stock PopperCam).

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — LOCK-ON FRAMING + DISTINCT CUTSCENE SYSTEM. A lock-on / two-target camera keeps subject AND target BOTH in frame with deliberate composition (camera positioned behind the player along the player->target axis, distance/FOV scaled by their separation so both stay readable at any range, eased/soft-lock interpolation so target-switch swings instead of snaps), AND a SEPARATE cutscene/sequence system (smooth multi-point path + eased FOV moves) distinct from the gameplay camera. The discriminator is whether the build commits to BOTH composed dual-subject lock-on AND a real cutscene path: passing requires (1) lock-on that FRAMES BOTH combatants — derive camera position behind the player along the player->target axis (not just pointing AT the enemy), scale distance/FOV by player<->target separation so both stay on screen, SOFT-lock by lerping the goal CFrame (~0.1) so switches swing smoothly, with line-of-sight validation (raycast excluding other characters) and an obstruction-break GRACE timer (~1-2s, don't drop the lock the instant a thin pillar blocks it) and limited free-look preserved while locked + an eased un-lock (not a hard snap back); AND (2) a cutscene system on a SMOOTH multi-point path (quadratic/cubic Bezier or an animated Motor6D camera rig, t eased through Sine/Quad InOut for accel/decel, look-at decoupled from the path so the lens holds a subject while the body sweeps) with entry/exit hygiene (Scriptable, Disconnect the render bind to end, Play(0) hard-cut, lock+restore player state + CameraType=Custom). A build that merely points at a target with no composition (snapping CFrame.lookAt at the enemy every frame, ignoring the player), or chains two-point CFrame:Lerp/Tween dollies for cutscenes (robotic slide, visible seams), FAILS. A build with composed soft-lock dual-framing AND a smooth-path cutscene PASSES; WorldToViewportPoint screen-space target placement (rule-of-thirds/headroom), dot-product/screen-center target selection with flick-to-switch + debounce, and frame-delta-averaged lock smoothing push toward full marks. A build with lock-on but no cutscene system (or a cutscene path but lock-on that just snaps at the enemy) earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The default camera has no concept of a combat target or a directed shot — lock-on is a whole context mode the stock follow cannot do, and naive lock-on hard-snaps CFrame.lookAt at the enemy every frame, which jerks violently on target switch and ignores the player entirely. The Soulslike difference is composition: position behind the player ALONG the player->target axis so both fighters are framed, scale distance/FOV by their separation so distant duels still frame both, SOFT-lock (lerp the goal, not snap), validate line-of-sight (raycast excluding other characters so a passerby doesn't steal the ray), and add an obstruction-break grace timer so brushing behind a thin pillar doesn't snap the camera off the boss — plus preserve limited free-look and ease the un-lock (unlocking commonly 'returns to previous positions in a disruptive, non-smooth manner'). On the cutscene side, a straight CFrame:Lerp between two points reads as a robotic slide with visible kinks when chained; Bezier arcs (or an animated Motor6D camera rig) + Quad/Sine-InOut easing + a look-at DECOUPLED from the path are real cinematography, and the production hygiene (Disconnect to actually end the loop, Play(0) hard-cut, full state save/restore) is what separates a finished sequence from a stuck/mushy camera. Eiserloh's hard-constraint Points-of-Focus vs soft Points-of-Interest with feathered weight is the pro shot-composition model. Grading composed-dual-lock-on AND a distinct smooth-path cutscene keeps it discriminating from point-at-target / two-point-dolly builds.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) lock-on that frames BOTH player and target — camera behind the player along the player->target axis, distance/FOV scaled by separation, soft-lock lerp of the goal CFrame on switch, line-of-sight raycast (excluding other characters), an obstruction-break grace timer (~1-2s), and preserved limited free-look + eased un-lock; AND (2) a distinct cutscene system on a smooth multi-point Bezier path (or animated Motor6D rig) with t eased Sine/Quad-InOut, look-at decoupled from the path, and entry/exit hygiene (Scriptable, Disconnect-to-end, Play(0) hard-cut, restore player + CameraType=Custom). WorldToViewportPoint screen-space placement (rule-of-thirds/headroom), dot-product target selection + flick-to-switch + debounce, and frame-delta-averaged smoothing are credited toward full marks. Merely pointing at a target with no composition, or chained two-point Lerp/Tween cutscenes, does NOT satisfy this; lock-on without a cutscene system, or a cutscene without composed lock-on, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: For lock-on: position the camera BEHIND the player along the player->target axis (so both are framed, not just lookAt at the enemy), scale distance/FOV by their separation, soft-lock by lerping the goal CFrame (~0.1) so target-switch swings, validate line-of-sight with a raycast excluding other characters, and add a ~1-2s obstruction-break grace timer plus limited free-look and an eased un-lock. For cutscenes: build a SEPARATE system — sample a multi-point quadratic/cubic Bezier (or animate a Motor6D camera rig in Moon Animator), ease t through Sine/Quad-InOut, decouple the look-at from the path, and on exit Disconnect the render bind, Play(0) to hard-cut in, and restore player state + CameraType=Custom.

grading.pass: Commits to BOTH composed dual-subject lock-on AND a real cutscene path: (1) lock-on that frames BOTH combatants — camera behind the player along the player->target axis, distance/FOV scaled by separation, soft-lock lerp of the goal CFrame on switch, line-of-sight raycast excluding other characters, an obstruction-break grace timer (~1-2s), preserved limited free-look + eased un-lock — AND (2) a distinct cutscene system on a smooth multi-point Bezier path (or animated Motor6D rig), t eased Sine/Quad-InOut, look-at decoupled from the path, with entry/exit hygiene (Scriptable, Disconnect-to-end, Play(0) hard-cut, restore player + CameraType=Custom). Full marks add WorldToViewportPoint screen-space placement, dot-product target selection + flick-to-switch + debounce, and frame-delta-averaged smoothing.
grading.partial: Has composed soft-lock dual-framing lock-on but NO distinct cutscene system, OR a smooth-path cutscene but lock-on that just snaps CFrame.lookAt at the enemy. One of the two required systems present and well-composed, the other missing.
grading.fail: Lock-on merely points at a target with no composition (snapping CFrame.lookAt at the enemy every frame, ignoring the player), AND/OR cutscenes are chained two-point CFrame:Lerp/Tween dollies (robotic slide, visible seams) — neither composed dual-framing nor a smooth multi-point path.
